assessments.rationale: Manufacturing with plastics can release microplastics and nanoplastics during the molding, cutting, and finishing stages of production (parameter (p), Page 80). Utilizing die-cast aluminum eliminates this risk of microplastic release in production, and reduces the carbon and material footprint of manufacturing (parameter (m), Page 33/80).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Use stage, as aluminum increases the weight of the screwdriver, reducing user ergonomics, and requires more energy to manufacture than plastics.

assessments.rationale: Using mechanical fasteners avoids the chemical emissions to air, water, or soil (parameter (q), Page 3/80) and the hazardous waste generation (parameter (r), Page 80) associated with adhesive bonding and chemical glues. It also consumes less energy during the assembly process compared to ultrasonic welding (parameter (g), Page 33).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Use stage, as mechanical fasteners can loosen over time under vibration, potentially reducing product durability compared to permanent chemical bonding.

assessments.rationale: Brushed DC motors have a simpler manufacturing process with fewer electronic components and rare-earth materials, which significantly reduces the material footprint (parameter (m), Page 33/80) and energy consumption during the manufacturing phase (parameter (g), Page 33), as well as minimizing the amounts of hazardous waste generated in production (parameter (r), Page 80).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Use stage, as brushless motors are much more energy-efficient and durable over their lifecycle, whereas brushed motors wear out faster and consume more energy during operation.

assessments.rationale: Passive heat sinks require no complex assembly, active electronics, or fluids, thereby minimizing the consumption of energy and resources in production (parameter (g), Page 33), preventing chemical emissions to air/water/soil from manufacturing cooling fluids (parameter (q), Page 3/80), and generating less production waste (parameter (r), Page 80).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Use stage, as passive cooling might limit the continuous power output or cause the screwdriver to overheat faster compared to active cooling, reducing functional performance.

assessments.rationale: A monolithic integrated design simplifies the production line, reducing the energy and resource consumption of the manufacturing process (parameter (g), Page 33) and minimizing the amounts of waste and scrap generated during assembly (parameter (r), Page 80).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Repairability and End-of-Life stages, as a monolithic design makes it extremely difficult to repair, refurbish, or recycle individual components, which goes against circularity but optimizes the immediate manufacturing footprint.

assessments.rationale: Manufacturing a corded AC power system avoids the highly resource-intensive and environmentally damaging production of lithium-ion batteries. This reduces the carbon/environmental footprint of manufacturing (parameter (m), Page 33/80), avoids the consumption of critical resources in production (parameter (g), Page 33), and prevents the generation of hazardous battery manufacturing waste (parameter (r), Page 80).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Use stage, as a corded screwdriver severely limits user mobility and portability compared to a cordless one, even though it is far superior from a manufacturing footprint perspective.
